1.note: This is the beginning of a new episode that takes place around twelve years after Abraham and King Abimelech made their treaty ([chapter 21](ta:21)). See how you translated “after those events” in Genesis [15:1](ta:15); it may be necessary to translate this phrase in a slightly different way here because of the different context. Alternate translation: [Sometime after those things happened] or [Several years later]
Make sure your translation of this clause does not sound like the test was over. Rather it introduces what the following episode is about. Alternate translation: [God wanted to test Abraham]
Make sure it is clear in your translation who is speaking here. Alternate translation: [Abraham replied to him]

Abraham is responding to God with the courteous expression that a person in this culture would use to tell a superior that he had heard a summons and was ready and willing to obey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Yes, Master?] or [What is it, Lord]

2.note: Translate this quote margin in a way that fits this context well. Alternate translation: [Then God said to him] or [Then God told him]

See how you translated **please** when God is talking to a person in Genesis 13:14; 15:5. Your translation of **take** here should not imply the use of force. See how you translated **took** in Genesis 11:31 and 12:5.

These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and it would be good to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation rather than combining them. It may be clearer in your language to connect the phrases with a word other than **and** in order to show that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [Please take your son, yes, your only son whom you love]
It is understood that he was to take Isaac with him. If this is not clear in your language, you could make that information explicit. Alternate translation: [and go with him]
Alternate translation: [to the region called Moriah] or [to the Moriah Region]
See how you translated a similar phrase in Genesis 8:20. Alternate translation: [and offer him there to me as a burnt offering] or [There you are to burn him up on an altar as a offering to me]
Alternate translation: [on top of one of the mountains] or [on top of a mountain]
Alternate translation: [that I will point out to you]

3.note: See how you translated **got up early in the morning** in Genesis 20:8. Alternate translation: [So the next morning, Abraham got up early] or [Early the next morning Abraham got up]

3.q: וַ⁠יִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י נְעָרָי⁠ו֙ אִתּ֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠אֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֑⁠וֹ
3.note: Alternate translation: [He took two of his servants with him and his son Isaac] or [Then he took his son Isaac and two of his servants]

The reason Abraham is the only one mentioned in this clause and in the next sentence is that he is in focus. He did not travel alone and he probably did not chop the wood alone. Decide whether or not you need to make that explicit in your translation. Alternate translation: [and he split some firewood with them] or [and they chopped some firewood together]

Some languages must translate this noun phrase using a verb. Do what is natural in your language. See what you did in verse 2. Alternate translation: [to use for the burnt offering and loaded it on the donkey] or [that they would use to burn the offering and loaded it on the donkey]

In this context, **got up** is used as an idiom that means Abraham started an activity. It does not mean that he was sitting down and literally stood up. Alternate translation: [Then he set out with them for the place] or [Then they started traveling to the mountain]
Alternate translation: [that God had told him to go to]

4.note: Alternate translation: [After walking for three days]
See how you translated the idiom **lifted his eyes** in Genesis 18:2. It may be necessary to translate it differently here, because of the different context. Alternate translation: [he looked up]

Consider where it is best in your language to put the location phrase **from a distance** or “in the distance.” Alternate translation: [and he could see the place where they were headed in the distance] or [and in the distance he could see the place where they were going]

5.note: Be consistent here with how you translated **young men** in verse 3. Alternate translation: [Then Abraham told his servants]
Some languages have special dual pronouns (that refer to only two people) that can be used in verse 5 to refer to Abraham’s two servants.

See how you translated **the boy** in Genesis 21:12, 17–20. We do not know for sure how old Isaac was at this time, but estimates range between 18 and 37 years old. Make sure your translation of **boy** allows for that fact. Alternate translation: [while the young man and I go]
Alternate translation: [over there to that mountain]

In that culture, people had the custom of bowing down to worship God. Make sure it is clear in your translation why Abraham and Isaac would bow down. Alternate translation: [and bow down to worship God]
Alternate translation: [Then we will return to you here] or [After that, we will come back here to you]

6.note: See how you translated **firewood** and **burnt offering** in verse 3. Alternate translation: [Then he took the firewood for the burnt offering off the donkey] or [Then he took the firewood that they would use to burn the sacrifice]

The Hebrew text does not specify exactly where Abraham put the wood on Isaac. Only specify that in a translation if it is necessary in your language. Alternate translation: [and gave it to his son Isaac to carry]

The **fire** can either refer to hot coals (in a pot) or to a flint stone and wood chips that they would use to start the fire on the altar. Make sure that your translation of this phrase does not mean that Abraham was holding fire or hot coals in his bare hands. Alternate translation: [a fire pot with hot embers in it] or [the other things to make a fire]
Some languages have a dual pronoun that could be used here. Alternate translation: [Then Abraham and Isaac walked on together] or [Then they continued walking toward the mountain]

7.note: Consider what is the best way to translate this quote margin in your language. Alternate translation: [and as they went Isaac said to his father Abraham]
Consider what is the best way to refer to Abraham at this point in the paragraph in your language. Alternate translation: [Abraham said to him]
See how you translated the idiom **Behold me** in [verse 1](ta:22). Alternate translation: [What is it, my son?]
Make sure that the way you translate this quote margin fits well with what Isaac says next.
Alternate translation: [the fire pot and the firewood] or [what we need to make a fire to burn the sacrifice]
Alternate translation: [for us to use as the burnt offering?] or [for us to burn as our sacrifice to God?] or [that we will burn as our offering to God?]

8.note: Alternate translation: [Then Abraham said to him]
**God will see for himself** is an idiom that means God will provide the lamb. Make sure this meaning is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [God himself will see to it that there is]
Consider whether it is more natural in your language to put this address first in this quote and say, “My son, God himself will …”
See how you translated **the two of them** in verse 6. Alternate translation: [So the two of them walked on together] or [So they continued walking together toward the mountain]

9.note: Alternate translation: [After they got to] or [After they arrived at] or [After they reached]
See how you translated this phrase in verse 3. Alternate translation: [the mountain that God had told him to go to]

Abraham arranged the wood on top of the altar so that it would burn well. Make sure your translation of this phrase does not sound like he lit the fire yet; he did not do that until verse 13 when he sacrificed the ram. Alternate translation: [and laid the wood on top of it]
Consider which order of these phrases is the clearest and most natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and put him on top of the wood that was on the altar]

10.note: Consider whether it is better in your language to use a noun or a pronoun to refer to Abraham here. See how you translated **knife** in verse 6. Alternate translation: [Then he took the knife in his hand]

In the process of sacrificing, the first step was to kill the sacrifice and then burn up the body on the altar. If necessary, you could make that information explicit in your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [in order to kill his son before sacrificing his body on the altar]

11.note: Make sure in your translation that it does not sound like Abraham killed Isaac. See how you translated this phrase in Genesis 21:17. Alternate translation: [But before Abraham could use the knife, an angel from Yahweh called]
The angel repeats Abraham’s name to communicate urgency and that he wants him to stop and listen. Make sure your translation does not sound like the angel was angry or criticizing Abraham.
Alternate translation: [Abraham replied to the angel]
See how you translated **Behold me** in [verse 1](ta:22). Alternate translation: [What is it, Master?] or [Yes, Master?]

12.note: Make sure it is clear in your translation that the angel is speaking here, not Abraham. Alternate translation: [Then the angel said]
Consider whether your language has an idiom that has the same meaning as the Hebrew idiom here. Alternate translation: [Do not lay your hands on] or [Do not kill]
See how you translated this in verse 5. Alternate translation: [the young man]

The angel repeats the previous command (using different words) in order to emphasize that Abraham should not hurt Isaac. Most languages can do something similar. Do what is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Do not do anything to harm him] or [You must not do anything to harm him] or [You must not harm him in any way]
Yahweh is the one talking here, represented by the angel who speaks on his behalf, or perhaps God is appearing to Abraham as an angel. Alternate translation: [Now I see] or [You have shown me]

Alternate translation: [because you obeyed me and did not hold back your son from me, yes your only son] or [because you obeyed me and did not refuse to sacrifice your son to me, even though he is your only son]

13.note: See how you translated **lifted his eyes and looked** in Genesis 18:2.
A ram is an adult male sheep or goat. See how you translated this term in Genesis 15:9. Alternate translation: [and suddenly he saw a ram behind him]
Alternate translation: [that had caught its horns in the thicket] or [that had its horns caught in a bush]

For some languages it may be necessary to explicitly state that Abraham untied Isaac and took him off the altar before he sacrificed the ram. Alternate translation: [So after releasing Isaac, he took the ram from the thicket] or [So he untied Isaac, went over to the ram and untangled it]

Animals that were sacrificed to God as burnt offerings were killed first before they were burned on an altar. Make sure your translation does not sound like the ram was burned alive. If that is not clear, you could make some of the above implied information explicit in your translation. Alternate translation: [Then he killed the ram and burned it on the altar as a offering to God]
Alternate translation: [as a substitute for his son]

14.note: Make sure it is clear that what Yahweh did in verse 13 is the reason that Abraham gave that place the name **Yahweh-Yireh** in verse 14. Alternate translation: [That is why Abraham called that place] or [Because God provided the ram, Abraham called that place]

If you include the meaning of this name in your translation text or in a footnote, be consistent with how you translate the verb “see/provide” in verse 8 (and later in verse 14), which the name is based on.
This refers to the time period when Moses was writing this book. If that is not clear, you could put that information in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Even now people still say]
See how you translated this idiom in verse 8. Alternate translation: [it will be provided by him] or [he will see to it that we have what we need] or [he will provide what we need]

15.q: וַ⁠יִּקְרָ֛א מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֑ם שֵׁנִ֖ית מִן־הַ⁠שָּׁמָֽיִם
15.note: See how you translated “called … from heaven” in verse 11, and how you translated **angel** in verses 11–12.

16.note: See how you translated **swear** in Genesis 21:23–24.

16.q: כִּ֗י יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ אֶת־הַ⁠דָּבָ֣ר הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה
16.note: Alternate translation: [that since you have done what I said] or [that since you obeyed me]
See how you translated a similar phrase in verse 12. Alternate translation: [and did not refuse to sacrifice your son to me] or [were willing to give your son to me]
See how you translated this in verse 12. Alternate translation: [even though he is your only son]

17.note: Alternate translation: [I will surely bless you] or [I will surely cause you to prosper greatly]
Alternate translation: [I will greatly increase the number of your descendants so that they will be] or [In fact, I will give you so many offspring that they will be]

Make sure it is clear in your translation that God is comparing the number of stars and grains of sand to the number of descendants Abraham will have. There will be so many that no one can count them all (as in Genesis 13:16 and 15:6). Alternate translation: [as many as the stars in the sky]
Alternate translation: [and as many as the grains of sand on the seashore]

Cities often had high stone walls surrounding them to protect the people inside. The gates in the walls were the only way to go in or out of a city. The idiom “possess the gates of … enemies” refers to taking control of the cities and conquering the people living there. Consider what is the best way to translate this idiom in your language. Alternate translation: [and they will conquer the cities of all their enemies] or [They will conquer all their enemies and rule over them] or [Your offspring will …]

18.note: See how you translated **offspring** in verse 17. Alternate translation: [In your offspring] or [Because of your offspring] or [By means of your offspring]
Make sure your translation of **my voice** refers to what God commanded Abraham. Alternate translation: [because you heeded my command]

19.note: Make sure your translation does not sound like Abraham returned alone (without Isaac). Alternate translation: [Afterwards Abraham and Isaac went back]
Be consistent here with how you translated **young men** in verses 3 and 5. Alternate translation: [to the two servants]

At that time, Abraham and his family were living in Beersheba (Genesis 21:31–34). So in your translation, it should not sound like Beersheba was a new destination; they were returning home. Alternate translation: [Then they returned home together to the city of Beersheba]

Make sure your translation does not sound like Abraham was living alone in Beersheba apart from his family. Alternate translation: [and Abraham continued to live there with his family] or [where Abraham and his family continued to live]

20.note: This phrase introduces a new topic. Consider what is the best way to do that in your language. Alternate translation: [Sometime after that]
Consider what is the best way to translate this passive clause in your language.
Alternate translation: [Listen] or [I have some news for you:]

20.q: יָלְדָ֨ה מִלְכָּ֥ה גַם־הִ֛וא בָּנִ֖ים לְ⁠נָח֥וֹר אָחִֽי⁠ךָ
20.note: For some languages it may be better to use an indirect quote in this verse and say, “Sometime later Abraham found out that his brother Nahor and Nahor’s wife Milcah had some sons,” Alternate translation: [Milcah the wife of your brother Nahor has born some sons for him] or [your brother Nahor and his wife Milcah also have some sons]

21.note: Alternate translation: [including their oldest son Uz, then Buz and Kemuel] or [The first one is Uz, the second is Buz, and the third is Kemuel]
Alternate translation: [who fathered Aram] or [whose son is Aram]

22.note: Make sure it is clear in your translation that the people listed in verse 22 were sons of Nahor and Milcah, not sons of Kemuel (verse 21).

22.q: כֶּ֣שֶׂד וְ⁠אֶת־חֲז֔וֹ וְ⁠אֶת־פִּלְדָּ֖שׁ וְ⁠אֶת־יִדְלָ֑ף וְ⁠אֵ֖ת בְּתוּאֵֽל
22.note: Consider whether it is best in your language to use a conjunction between each name in this list (like Hebrew does), or only before the last name in the list. See what you did for a similar list of names in Genesis 10:26–29.

23.note: Some translations put this sentence in parentheses to show that it is a separate comment by the author and not part of the previous quote. Also, see how you translated **fathered** in Genesis 11:27. Alternate translation: [Bethuel was the father of Rebekah]

24.note: Alternate translation: [In addition to that, Nahor and his concubine Reumah also had some sons, including]
See how you connected the list of names in verse 22.
